transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

This symptom—where the microwave stops but the clock stays on, and nudging the door restarts it—is a common sign of an intermittent electrical fault in the door interlock system. The microwave has safety switches that cut power if the door isn't perfectly latched; if one of these is worn or the latch mechanism is slightly misaligned, it can break the circuit momentarily. Before we consider internal repairs (which require opening the casing and are not safe to do yourself), please check the physical latch. With the microwave unplugged, look at the plastic hooks on the door edge and the slots in the frame. Is there any food or grease blocking them, and do the hooks look intact? If they are clean and undamaged, it is likely a worn interlock switch inside that needs an engineer to replace.

There was some grease around the door hooks and latch slots, so I cleaned it off. It's still happened once since. Hooks look intact. The door might sit very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't be sure. No smell, sparks or tripping.

These switches cut power if they don't feel a firm latch; if the switch is worn or the door isn't pressing it firmly enough, it cuts out randomly. 1. Does the door feel loose or wobbly when you gently push it?
2. Can you see if there is a gap between the door and the frame that looks wider at the bottom than at the top? If the door feels loose or misaligned, the latch mechanism may be worn or the hinges shifted, preventing the switch from engaging fully. If it feels tight but still fails, the internal switch itself has likely failed and will need an engineer to replace.

It doesn't feel loose or wobbly as far as I can tell. The door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, but I can't say for sure whether the gap is wider at the bottom. It does seem to cut out more when I close the door gently rather than firmly.

These switches cut power if they don't feel a firm, secure latch; if the contacts inside are worn or sticking, they break the circuit momentarily when the door is closed softly. Because fixing this requires opening the microwave casing to access the mains-powered interlock switches, I cannot advise you on how to do this safely. You should contact a qualified appliance engineer to replace the faulty switch(es). In the meantime, try to close the door firmly and consistently to keep using it, but be aware it may stop again at any time.
